validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: unambiguous. Texas Gas Transmission is a major, long-documented interstate gas trunk line: Wikipedia infobox (Founded 1948, Owensboro KY HQ, Parent Boardwalk Pipeline Partners LP, FERC code 18), Boardwalk's own current subsidiary page (bwpipelines.com/subsidiaries/texas-gas-transmission/home, live 2026), two SEC 10-K annual reports on EDGAR (FY2004 and FY2005, filed by registrant 'Texas Gas Transmission, LLC', CIK 97452), and active 2025-2026 FERC dockets (Dearborn County Lateral CP26-536, Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project referenced on Boardwalk's own site) all describe the same physical system. Not a GEM-only entity.
CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an operating natural-gas transmission pipeline (interstate FERC Natural Gas Act company, not a gathering/process line).
DUPLICATE: checked against the full 37-row Gulf Coast roster -- no other row is this system under another name (its route, Louisiana to Indiana/Illinois/Ohio, is far longer and geographically distinct from every other Gulf Coast intrastate/offshore line in the batch). Not a duplicate/relabel candidate.
STATUS ('operating'): confirmed current -- Boardwalk's live 2026 subsidiary page describes active throughput, an active project (Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project) and a 24/7 emergency line; a FERC docket (CP26-536, filed 2026-06-18) shows Texas Gas actively expanding the system. Two independent origins (Boardwalk company site; Federal Register/EnergyDocket coverage of the FERC docket).
ATTRIBUTION: the sheet's StartState/Province value 'Louisana' is a TYPO for 'Louisiana' -- flagged as a data-quality (attribution) issue, corrected in the paired Location fill below (sourced to Wikipedia, the SEC 10-Ks, and marcellusdrilling.com, which independently agree the route runs Louisiana <-> Ohio via Arkansas, Mississippi, Tennessee, Kentucky, Indiana and Illinois). Owner1 'Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' 100% is confirmed as the direct parent entity (Wikipedia's 'Boardwalk Pipelines' article infobox names 'Boardwalk Pipeline Partners, LP' as the operating partnership; Boardwalk's own site). Note for the record: the ULTIMATE parent is Loews Corporation (Boardwalk Pipeline Partners LP was taken private by Loews in 2018; Wikipedia's current infobox lists Parent = Loews Corporation, and offshore-technology.com/GlobalData's ownership chart shows 100% Loews). This is a holding-chain nuance, not an error -- 'Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' remains the correct immediate-parent name and is left as-is; flagging only so a reviewer can decide whether to record Loews as an added ultimate-owner note.
Discovery lead (not a roster PID, noted for the orchestrator): Texas Gas Transmission filed FERC docket CP26-536 (2026-06-18) for a new ~12-mile, 20-inch, $86.2M 'Dearborn County Lateral' delivering to Vistra's Miami Fort power plant in Ohio -- a physically distinct new lateral, not yet in GEM under any PID in this roster. Also active: an 'Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project' (compressor/reliability upgrade, southwest Louisiana) named on Boardwalk's own site, and an April 2025 open season for +2 Bcf/d of Marcellus/Utica-to-Gulf capacity (marcellusdrilling.com) which appears to be the driver behind the jump from the pipeline's historical ~2.8-4.3 Bcf/d capacity to the ~6.1-6.3 Bcf/d figure now current. None of these were researched as separate stageable rows here (out of scope for a validity pass on P0263's Main Line record) but are worth a Discovery look.
Sources opened: 10 of 10 harvested wiki_citations.json entries were checked live (bit.ly redirect, 2 SEC EDGAR filings, txgt.com subsidiary page + root, offshore-technology.com, eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php navigation page, fractracker.org, and the two Clarksville TN eminent-domain news stories) plus 4 open-web sources found independently (Wikipedia x2, marcellusdrilling.com, hartenergy.com via Wayback). eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php is a navigation page (per batch guidance) -- not usable as a ref for any value. The two Clarksville, TN news stories (2014, 2017) concern local eminent-domain disputes over a Texas Gas lateral in Montgomery County TN; they corroborate the pipeline's real-world presence/activity but state no numeric spec values usable for this row's fills, so they were not cited as refs (kept only as existence corroboration in this note).

fills.researcher_notes: MATERIAL TIMING NOTE, not a plain confirmation: two 2004/2005 SEC 10-Ks (both on EDGAR, CIK 97452) and a 2011 Hart Energy article (via Wayback) all give a materially LOWER historical mainline delivery capacity of ~2.8 Bcf/d (2,800 MMcf/d) -- roughly 55% below the sheet's 6,100 MMcf/d. That gap is explained, not contradicted, by Boardwalk's April 2025 open season for +2 Bcf/d of new Marcellus/Utica-to-Gulf capacity (marcellusdrilling.com) plus further growth reflected in Boardwalk's current (2026) site stating a 6.3 Bcf/d peak-day delivery record. Net: the sheet's 6,100 MMcf/d value is plausible as a CURRENT figure and is corroborated within ~3% by Boardwalk's own current disclosure, but neither source states exactly '6,100' -- 'peak day delivery' and a nameplate/certificated 'capacity' are not strictly the same metric. Recommend keeping the value but treating this as medium- rather than high-confidence pending a primary FERC tariff capacity figure. Do NOT use the 2.8 Bcf/d SEC/Hart Energy figures as the current capacity -- they are stale (pre-2025-expansion) and were not staged as an alternative value.

Per gem_schema.md's FuelSource gotcha, this field wants a single named upstream field/plant, not a generic description. Texas Gas Transmission is a multi-source interstate trunk with dozens of interconnects: Boardwalk's own site names supply from 'production areas in Arkansas, Louisiana and Texas, as well as indirectly from Pennsylvania, Ohio and West Virginia', shale plays 'Fayetteville, Haynesville, Marcellus and Utica', hub interconnects at 'Perryville Exchange, Lebanon, Henry Hub and Carthage', plus conventional wellhead supply. No single named field or plant is the line's source -- left blank per the schema note ('if you can't attribute one, leave it blank and note why') rather than defaulting to 'Natural Gas' or forcing one hub name.
